the study of the phenomenological impact of the trilinear neutral gauge couplings in the context of the effective Lagrangians.
the study of the trilinear neutral gauge-boson couplings in the context of the effective field theory approach.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trilinear neutral couplings may be a very interesting probe of new physics, but only in specific situations.
the trilinear neutral gauge couplings are not expected to play any significant role in precision measurements, unless a nonlinear realization of the gauge symmetry is considered.
trilinear neutral boson couplings can be a useful tool in the search for new physics at the LHC, but only if the latter respects some specific symmetries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the trilinear neutral gauge couplings can be a useful probe of new physics in the nonlinear realization of the $\mathrm{SU(2)}_{\mathrm L}\mathrm{}\ifmmote\texttimes{}\mathrm{}\mathrm{}$U(1)$\mathrm{)}_{\rm Y}$ gauge symmetry.

, in the linear case, trilinear neutral gauge couplings are suppressed by at least a factor $v^{2}/M{,}^{2}$ where M is the new physics scale, while in the nonlinear scenario they can be of the same order as the quartic neutral gauge boson coupling.
trilinear couplings of neutral gauge bosons can be generated at tree level by dimension-6 effective operators in the nonlinear case and by dimension-8 in the linear case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of trilinear neutral gauge couplings in the effective theory is a clear signature of nonlinearly realized gauge symmetries.
the presence of a light Higgs boson is crucial to have sizable trilinear couplings in the linear realization of the gauge symmetry.
the nonlinear scenario is the most promising to look for the presence of these couplings in the near future.
